events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Dallam County in the panhandle of Texas...
North Central Hartley County in the panhandle of Texas...

* WHEN...Until 230 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1131 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dalhart.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Smyth County in southwestern Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 330 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1226 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Crewey Branch, Middle Fork Holston River, Lynn Camp Creek, Hungry
Mother Creek, North Fork Holston River, Campbell Creek, Beaver
Creek and Lick Creek. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1
inch are expected over the area. This additional rain will result
in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hungry Mother State Park, Broadford and Nebo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
At 1118 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 4
miles south of Dalhart, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Dalhart, Hartley, and Conlen.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The western and central Oklahoma Panhandle, along with the
northwest Texas Panhandle.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeat rounds of heavy rain could result in flooding and flash
flooding in the northwest combined Panhandles.
